This is the actual printed pod list from [diagnostic run 39228810620](https://github.com/somehowchris/tika-indra-ocr-client/actions/runs/39228810620). Its generic `List` metadata has an empty resource version even though the sole ready pod has version `639`. The strict gate stopped before runtime-container admission or OCR; readiness is not lifecycle acceptance. The original bytes and identities are retained in `provenance.json`.

The pinned [kubectl generic printer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bb826b1d48562f110659e64e8ec444327433db95/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/get/get.go) constructs this list after flattening resources. The gate now requests the namespaced PodList with `get --raw`, preserving the server's list resource version for its existing exact-UID watch. It retains the same timeout, selector and strict numeric resource-version check. It does not substitute the pod item's version.

A local reproduction using the checksum-pinned kubectl and a synthetic loopback API returned the same empty printed list metadata; `--raw` preserved the complete synthetic server response. That demonstrates the client behavior, not a real-cluster or lifecycle result. A fresh focused CI replay must pass the remaining gates.
